result:
**The proposed answer $r$ is almost certainly wrong. The ratio should be $1$.**

The proposed solution gives no derivation. It cites a "finite-slope multiplicity result" that it does not state, and I cannot verify one that gives linear growth in $r$.

The closest analogue is Hida's control theorem for classical modular forms. The ordinary part of $M_k(\Gamma_1(Np^r))$ has rank independent of $r\ge 1$, equal to the rank at level $\Gamma_1(Np)$. Finite-slope eigensystems in the Drinfeld setting behave similarly. I believe the Dalal–Kumar results on Drinfeld cuspforms of level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^m)$ state that the multiplicity of such an eigensystem $\lambda$ does not depend on the $\wp$-power $r$ once $r\ge 1$. That would make the ratio $1$, not $r$.

The linear-in-$r$ growth in the proposal resembles the classical count of $p$-old forms for a newform of level prime to $p$. That count does not apply to finite-slope eigensystems already at level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp)$, where $\wp$ divides the level.

I have not checked the exact theorem statement against the literature, so this rests on the Hida-type analogy and my recollection of the Drinfeld results. The proposed derivation supplies no argument that would support $r$.

VERDICT: REJECT
